title: Supabase (PostgreSQL + pgvector, free tier) benchmark failure analysis
summary: Supabase could not reliably complete the benchmark. The 4096-dimensional embeddings exceed pgvector's ANN index limits, forcing exact sequential-scan search. On the free-tier Nano compute instance, each query reads ~300 MB from disk, which exhausts the instance's burstable disk I/O budget during sustained runs. Query latency then degrades from seconds to over 10 minutes, triggering PostgreSQL statement_timeout cancellations, and the overloaded instance intermittently kills connections during store initialization.

environment.compute_instance: Nano (shared CPU, ~0.5 GB RAM, burstable disk I/O)

dataset.total_size: 1077 MB (heap 65 MB; vectors TOASTed, ~16 KB per row)

root_causes.cause: 4096-dimensional vectors cannot be ANN-indexed by pgvector
root_causes.detail: pgvector HNSW supports at most 2000 dimensions for the vector type and 4000 for halfvec. The native 4096-dim embedding therefore forces exact nearest-neighbor search: a full scan computing cosine distance against every vector in the target collection (17,480 rows / ~286 MB for the main collection) on every query.

root_causes.cause: Working set does not fit in free-tier RAM
root_causes.detail: Each query must detoast ~286 MB of vector data. The Nano instance (~0.5 GB RAM) cannot cache it, so every query re-reads it from disk. pg_stat_statements recorded ~136 GB of cumulative disk block reads over 454 benchmark queries (~300 MB per query).

The free-tier instance has a small burstable disk I/O budget that refills slowly and is shared across runs. Once depleted during a sustained run, the same query degrades from ~0.7-20 s to 8.5+ minutes. This explains why one run survived 5 hours (2026-07-16) while the next failed in under 1 hour (2026-07-17): the second run started with an already-drained budget.

Supabase's default session statement_timeout is 2 minutes. Throttled exact-scan queries exceeded it (first failure: speed-test query 5). After raising the timeout to 10 minutes via a per-connection SET, a later query still exceeded 10 minutes under throttling (second failure: speed-test query 42). Worst-case latency under I/O throttling is effectively unbounded, so no fixed timeout guarantees completion.

root_causes.cause: Transient connection loss during store initialization
root_causes.detail: Error at 2026-07-17 06:15: '(EDBHANDLEREXITED) connection to database closed' on 'select pg_catalog.version()' while PGVector.__init__ opened its first connection. The database itself did not restart (uptime ~13 h at diagnosis; 12 of 60 backends in use), indicating a single Supavisor backend handler died on the overloaded instance, likely under memory pressure. This dropped Supabase from the scalability phase of that run.

measured_evidence.note: Cancelled statements are not recorded by pg_stat_statements, so true worst-case latency exceeds the 512.9 s maximum shown for completed queries.

failure_timeline.event: Benchmark run sustained ~5 hours before stopping; speed-test query cancelled by the default 2-minute statement_timeout (psycopg.errors.QueryCanceled at query 5).
Fixes applied: statement_timeout raised to 10 min per connection, btree index added on langchain_pg_embedding.collection_id, single query verified at ~22 s.
Next run failed in under 1 hour at speed-test query 42: QueryCanceled despite the 10-minute timeout, due to disk I/O throttling from the already-depleted burst budget.
Store initialization failed with (EDBHANDLEREXITED) connection to database closed; Supabase dropped from the scalability phase of that run.

mitigations_applied: Per-connection SET statement_timeout (default 600000 ms) via SQLAlchemy connect event in utils/cloud_vector_stores.create_supabase_engine, applied so it survives the Supavisor pooler
btree index ix_langchain_pg_embedding_collection_id so per-collection scans do not touch other collections' rows
Speed test records a failed Supabase query and continues instead of aborting the whole run
Top-K sensitivity and corpus scalability phases warn and skip a failed Supabase level instead of aborting the whole run
statement_timeout value recorded in exported run metadata (database_limitations.Supabase.statement_timeout_ms)

decision.outcome: Supabase excluded from full benchmark runs (checkbox left unselected).
decision.rationale: The free-tier compute instance cannot sustain unindexed 4096-dimensional exact nearest-neighbor search at this corpus size: latency varies from 0.7 s to over 10 minutes within a single run depending on the remaining disk I/O budget, making results non-reproducible and runs unreliable. The collected partial data is reported as a platform-limitation finding.
decision.expected_on_paid_tier: A Small/Medium compute instance (2-4 GB RAM) could cache the ~1 GB table, stabilizing queries at consistent single-digit seconds without throttling; search would remain exact and therefore still the slowest of the evaluated databases.
